title: The Shiva Purana — books one and seven
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa like the other Puranas. The text as it survives is the product of the Shaiva communities of northern India, compiled and enlarged over several centuries.
description: The Shiva Purana is the great narrative scripture of Shiva: the creation and the dissolution of the worlds, the linga, the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice, the marriage of Shiva and Parvati, the birth and wars of Skanda and Ganesha, the deeds of the avatars and the great pilgrimage centres. It teaches the worship of the linga and the observance of the days and vows of the Shaiva year.
historicalContext: The Purana the Shaiva Siddhanta and the Shaiva traditions of north India read: its seven samhitas collect older material, and its teaching on devotion to Shiva shaped temple worship and pilgrimage across the subcontinent.
availabilityNote: Partial: the GRETIL e-text carries books one and seven only, in the edition of the Anandashrama, and they are streamed at read time one chapter at a time. Books two to six are not published in this transcription and the work is not claimed as complete; the availability note is part of the record rather than a defect of the import.
